question: _______ of the Constitution of India provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 22.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution **provides protection against such arrest and detention inserted **in cases in preventive detention under** Section 151** of the Criminal Procedure Code** 1973.**
 
• Preventive detention is without trial. A person can be detained only on grounds of suspicion hence the rights of a person arrested in this manner get governed by preventive detention laws.
 
• Preventive detention is an action taken on grounds of suspicion some wrong actions may be done by the person concerned hence a **Police officer can arrest an individual without orders from a magistrate without a warrant **if he gets any information of such an individual cannot commit any offence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience, the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate religion to all citizens.
 
• **Article 23** in the Constitution Of India 1949 means **Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour**. 
 
• **The Right against Exploitation is enshrined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution**. 
 
• **Article 20**, no person shall be convicted of any offense except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.
